source.work: Drizzle ORM documentation, PostgreSQL table definition
source.locator: pgTable with primaryKey on the id column
source.paraphrase: Give every pgTable an explicit primary key on its id column. A text or uuid id without primaryKey is a heap with no identity: updates and deletes have no row to aim at.

invariants.why: Without a primary key, two rows can share an id and no constraint stops them. Deletes and updates by id hit an arbitrary row.
invariants.fixHint: Chain .primaryKey() onto the id column, or declare the composite key the domain needs.
invariants.avoid: The rule recognizes text("id") and uuid("id") without primaryKey. serial("id") and integer("id") without primaryKey, and a key declared on a differently named column, are shapes this rule does not see.

source.work: Drizzle ORM documentation, PostgreSQL column types and indexes & constraints
source.locator: serial, integer identity columns and primaryKey; https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/column-types/pg and https://orm.drizzle.team/docs/indexes-constraints#primary-key
source.paraphrase: Declare the primary key explicitly with .primaryKey() or a composite primaryKey(). serial and identity columns only generate values; neither adds a primary key constraint.

invariants.why: An auto-incrementing id looks like an identity, but without a primary key nothing stops a manual insert or a restored backup from duplicating it, and updates by id can hit several rows.
invariants.fixHint: Chain .primaryKey() onto the id column, as in integer().primaryKey().generatedAlwaysAsIdentity(), or declare the composite key in the table's third argument.
invariants.avoid: unique() or generatedAlwaysAsIdentity() is not a primary key. The rule reads pgTable calls whose id column, named "id" or keyed id:, is serial, bigserial, smallserial, integer, bigint or smallint; any primaryKey in the table passes. text and uuid ids belong to DRIZ-TABLE-001.

source.locator: timestamp with the mode and withTimezone options
source.paraphrase: Declare how a timestamp crosses the boundary: mode date, string, or number, and withTimezone where the domain needs it. A bare timestamp leaves the driver to guess, and two drivers guess differently.

invariants.why: A timestamp with no mode shifts by the session timezone on read or write. Events move by hours and nobody touched them.
invariants.fixHint: Pass { mode: "date" } (or string/number), and add withTimezone: true when the instant must carry its zone.
invariants.avoid: Other options such as precision or defaultNow do not satisfy the rule; only mode or withTimezone counts. date columns are a different type this rule does not see.

source.locator: relations with one(), fields, and references
source.paraphrase: A one() relation must name its fields and references so the join has columns to use. one() with no fields, or with an empty config, declares a relation that points nowhere.

invariants.why: A dangling relation compiles and fails at query time, or joins on a guess. The error arrives in production, not at definition.
invariants.fixHint: Pass { fields: [...], references: [...] } to one(), or use many() when the other side needs no key.
invariants.avoid: many() without fields passes: only one() needs the key pair. A fields array that names the wrong columns still passes; the rule checks presence, not correctness.
